learningObjectiveItems.learningObjective: This learning lab will enable you to explore specific aspects of the following chapter objectives within the context of a typical healthcare scenario:

introductionList: You have just graduated from a physical therapy assistant program in Virginia and have been recently hired by Madison Valley Hospital in Wisconsin. One of your assignments is to ambulate Ms. Jones, in room 221, 100 feet as tolerated; at 1000 and 1400. She may use a walker as needed to assist with ambulation. You are running behind schedule for her morning appointment and arrive at her room at 1030.
You have been working with her for several days, so you know that she is motivated to walk, and you are eager to get started so that she stays on her planned ambulation schedule.

STEP_1.instructions: It's the start of the HOSA chapter meeting. Members are scattered around, chatting and laughing. The president stands at the front, trying to regain control of the room.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint, if you need guidance.
STEP_1.question: How should the president call the meeting to order?
STEP_1.CORRECT: The president bangs the gavel and says, "The meeting will now come to order."
STEP_1.INCORRECT_1: The president bangs the gavel and raises his voice to be heard and states, "Hey everyone, let's quiet down and get started."
STEP_1.INCORRECT_2: The president bangs the gavel on the table and says, "It's time to start the meeting."

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks formality and structure.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks formality and structure.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The meeting should be formally called to order to establish that it has begun.

ThinkAbout: Why is it important to have a clear signal that a meeting has officially started?
How does calling a meeting to order help set the tone for the session?
AskYourself: How would members know when to focus if there is no formal start?
What happens to group discipline if meetings start informally?

STEP_1.reportRational: The president bangs the gavel once and announces, "The meeting will come to order."

STEP_2.instructions: Members stop talking. The room is quiet and attentive, recognizing the meeting has formally begun. It is now time to take the roll call.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint, if you need guidance.
STEP_2.question: What should the president and secretary do?
STEP_2.CORRECT: The secretary announces, "I will now read the names aloud of those who are present," or passes around a sign-in sheet for students to sign.
STEP_2.INCORRECT_1: The president looks around the room and asks, "Is everybody here? It looks like we have everyone, so let's get started. Secretary, please document everyone's names in the meeting notes."
STEP_2.INCORRECT_2: The secretary states to the president, "It looks like everyone is here. You can get started, and I will take a head count."

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks the structure and formal documentation needed to properly verify attendance.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. A head count alone does not provide the formality or accountability required in a proper roll call.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. Taking a roll call is important to document who is present and to ensure a quorum is met for the meeting.

ThinkAbout: Why is it important to document who is present at a formal meeting?
How does attendance tracking support transparency and decision-making?
AskYourself: If the attendance isn't tracked, can the group's decisions truly represent everyone?
What are my responsibilities in maintaining accurate records as a student leader?

STEP_2.reportRational: Taking a roll call is important to document who is present and to ensure a quorum is met.

STEP_3.instructions: The meeting progresses ahead. The president then gestures to the secretary to share the minutes of the previous meeting.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint, if you need guidance.
STEP_3.question: What should the secretary and the president do?
STEP_3.CORRECT: The secretary announces, "I will now read the minutes aloud," or provides copies of the minutes and pending issues to the attendees. The president asks, "Any corrections?" If there are no corrections, the minutes are approved.
STEP_3.INCORRECT_1: The secretary says, "A copy of the previous meeting minutes was distributed to all attendees to refer to before the meeting. Let's discuss any pending issues and then get started with whatever is on everyone's mind." The president agrees and moves ahead with the next item on the agenda.
STEP_3.INCORRECT_2: The secretary states, "We discussed the fundraiser for next month. Carlos motioned that we should do a mitten drive, but we ran out of time to vote on it. We should vote, then confirm if minutes are approved, and move on to new business."

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It does not maintain transparency and continuity of the meetings, as there is no call for corrections or formal approval of the minutes.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It jumps ahead to new business without formally reviewing or approving the full minutes, which can lead to confusion or missed corrections.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The minutes should be read aloud or copies of it should be provided to ensure all members agree on what was discussed and decided previously.

ThinkAbout: Why is it important to have a shared, written record of what was discussed and decided previously?
How do minutes help a group stay organized and accountable over time?
AskYourself: Why is it important to ask for corrections on previous decisions before moving ahead to discuss new business?
What role do meeting minutes play in preventing confusion or miscommunication?

STEP_3.reportRational: The minutes should be read aloud or copies of previous minutes should be provided to ensure all members agree on what was discussed and decided previously.

STEP_4.instructions: The president moves the meeting forward to discuss the next item on the agenda. He asks the treasurer to present his report to all the gathered members.
instructionsList: Choose the appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_4.question: How should the treasurer present his report?
STEP_4.CORRECT: We spent $210.25 on supplies for the bake sale. We made $748.76 on sales at the bake sale last week. Our current account balance is $6,461.80.
STEP_4.INCORRECT_1: We spent some money on supplies for the bake sale and earned a good amount through sales. Our current account balance is $6,461.80.
STEP_4.INCORRECT_2: We made a profit on the bake sale. I checked with the school bookkeeper, and our current account balance is $6,461.80.

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks integrity and responsibility in following basic financial reporting procedures in a team like sharing details of income and expenses.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It provides vague information and does not document specific earnings or expenses, which is essential for transparency and accountability in financial reporting.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The treasurer's report should include all details of the committee's expenses, earnings, and profits so that they are accurately filed and audited to ensure the team's budget is maintained.

ThinkAbout: Why is it important for organizations to keep a record of money coming in and going out?
What role does financial transparency play in a team or organizational setting?
AskYourself: Would you as a member feel confident making decisions about funds without clear financial information?
How would you justify the team's spending if someone in authority asked for details later?

STEP_4.reportRational: The treasurer's report should include all details of the committee's expenses, earnings, and profits so that they are accurately filed and audited to ensure the team's budget is maintained.

STEP_5.instructions: Following the treasurer's report, the president asks if there are any questions from the members. As there are no questions the treasurer's report is filed for audit. The president then asks the officers to share their updates with the members. There's an awkward silence as the members wait for someone to speak.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint, if you need guidance.
STEP_5.question: What should the officers do?
STEP_5.CORRECT: The secretary announces, "I would like to read you a thank you note from a recipient of our recent charity event."
STEP_5.INCORRECT_1: The officers consult briefly with one another and then state, "We have nothing to report."
STEP_5.INCORRECT_2: The vice president announces, "I don't have anything major to report. We still need a few ideas for the spring fundraiser."

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It shows a lack of initiative in fulfilling leadership duties and keeping the group informed.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It misses an opportunity to provide meaningful updates and lacks structure, shifting from reporting to brainstorming.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The report of officers is important to ensure transparent and regular communication within the committee.

ThinkAbout: What is the purpose of having officers give reports during a meeting?
How do reports from officers support transparency and follow-up?
AskYourself: What message does it send to other members when leaders have nothing to report?
How can regular reporting of officers strengthen a team's trust and accountability?

STEP_5.reportRational: The report of officers is important to ensure transparent and regular communication within the committee.

STEP_6.instructions: After the officers share their report, the president stands up again to address the members and move the meeting forward. He requests the standing committee chair to present his reports.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate response for the standing committee chair from the three options provided at the bottom of the screen.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_6.question: How should the standing committee chair present his reports?
STEP_6.CORRECT: The pet drive was successful. 500 lbs. of pet food was donated to the local shelter. We are still awaiting final administrative approval for our first aid kit fundraiser.
STEP_6.INCORRECT_1: Mei was in charge of our recent community event but she isn't here today. She plans to share her report at our next meeting.
STEP_6.INCORRECT_2: The pet drive was successful. I spoke with Mei, and she mentioned that a significant amount of pet food was donated to the local shelter.

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks preparation, and undermines the committee's responsibility and initiative to keep the organization informed.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It relies on secondhand information rather than a formal, prepared report from the committee chair.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The standing committees reports should be well-prepared and detailed as these committees stay the same each year. This helps maintain transparency and keep the organization updated on ongoing initiatives.

ThinkAbout: How can regular updates from committees support smooth planning and follow-through?
How do clear reports impact the team's ability to make informed decisions?
AskYourself: If a committee member is absent or unreachable, what is your role as another committee member in ensuring the team stays informed?
What message does it send when committee members come unprepared to report?

STEP_6.reportRational: The standing committees reports should be well-prepared and detailed as these committees stay the same each year. This helps maintain transparency and keep the organization updated on ongoing initiatives.

STEP_7.instructions: The president asks the special committee to present their reports. The celebrations committee chair is called up front to share details about the preparations for next week's party.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate response for the celebration committee chair from the three options provided at the bottom of the screen.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_7.question: How should the celebration committee chair present her reports?
STEP_7.CORRECT: Everything is in order for next week's celebration. We have a room reserved, the food has been ordered, and Mrs. Yovine will be picking up decorations.
STEP_7.INCORRECT_1: The party is next week, but we have hit a snag in securing the venue. Somehow, the dates were mixed up. Maybe we can reschedule it?
STEP_7.INCORRECT_2: We are facing some hurdles and need some help. Can someone help us with the decorations for the celebration? Mrs. Yovine said she will pick them up.

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It shows a lack of responsibility, integrity, and initiative on the part of the celebrations committee chair.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It shows a lack of preparation and shifts responsibility to the group instead of presenting a clear and complete report.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The special committee reports are presented in a responsible and clear manner by the representatives or chair of any special committee that has been formed such as a field trip or a special party.

ThinkAbout: What expectations and responsibilities come with leading or being part of a special committee?
How do clear updates from committees affect the success of group initiatives?
AskYourself: If you're trusted with a specific task, how should you prepare to report on it to your team?
What message does your preparedness (or lack of it) send to others in the organization?

STEP_7.reportRational: The special committee reports are presented in a responsible and clear manner by the representatives or chair of any special committee that has been formed such as a field trip or a special party.

STEP_8.instructions: The next item on the meeting's agenda is to discuss any unfinished business. The members look tired and seem impatient to leave the meeting.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_8.question: What should the president do?
STEP_8.CORRECT: The president calls for order in the meeting and reviews the previous meeting's notes. He states, "We still need to decide on a fundraiser for our HOSA expenses this year." A motion is made to have a car wash. It is seconded, and approved after a vote.
STEP_8.INCORRECT_1: The president reviews the previous meeting's notes and bangs the gavel for order. He states, "Alright, we will move to discuss unfinished business in the next meeting." The president moves forward with the next item for discussion on the meeting's agenda.
STEP_8.INCORRECT_2: The president reviews the previous meeting's notes. "We didn't finish talking about what we want to do for the fundraiser. We can talk about that in our next meeting. Meeting adjourned." The members feel relieved and begin leaving the meeting premise.

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It shows a lack of effective and decisive leadership, initiative, and a team player attitude.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It misses the opportunity to take action and delays important decisions, showing weak follow-through as a leader.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. Discussing unfinished business is important as it includes any issues from a previous meeting that could not be resolved at that time. These issues are presented one at a time in an orderly fashion.

ThinkAbout: Why might it be important to revisit and discuss unresolved topics from earlier meetings?
How does structured follow-through impact a team's goals?
AskYourself: What message does it send when a team avoids addressing unfinished matters?
What role does the presiding officer play in keeping discussions organized and on track?

STEP_8.reportRational: Unfinished business includes any issues from a previous meeting that could not be resolved at that time and these issues are presented one at a time in an orderly fashion.

STEP_9.instructions: The president invites all members to discuss new businesses and initiatives for the group. Excitement builds quickly, and several members begin talking at once, eager to get their suggestions heard.
instructionsList: Sort the actions shown on the screen in the correct order to depict the right parliamentary method to pass motions and hold a vote.
Tap on an action to select it, and then tap on a slot to place it.
To remove an action from a slot. select the Remove button.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_9.OPTION_1: A member makes a motion to have HOSA Spirit Day. The president asks for a second.
STEP_9.OPTION_2: Another member seconds it. The motion is restated and opened for discussion.
STEP_9.OPTION_3: Members suggest to wear HOSA t-shirts, purple socks and send text invites to seniors.
STEP_9.OPTION_4: The president notes this and suggests a separate motion. No more discussion follows.
STEP_9.OPTION_5: A vote is called. All members in favor say "Aye." There are no "Nays."
STEP_9.OPTION_6: The motion carries to have HOSA Spirit Day next Thursday.

INCORRECT.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT.text: You haven't sorted each action in the correct order. Select the Retry button to try again.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: You have sorted each action in the correct order.

ThinkAbout: Make sure a motion is clearly stated before discussion.
Always get a "second" before moving forward.
Allow time for discussion and suggestions.
Restate the motion before voting.
Record the decision of the vote fairly.
AskYourself: What is the proper sequence for making and passing a motion?
How does following parliamentary procedure ensure fairness in decision-making?

STEP_10.instructions: As the meeting draws to a close, the president moves on to address any upcoming programs and announcements. The group looks tired and ready to wrap things up.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_10.question: How should the president make his announcement?
STEP_10.CORRECT: We have scheduled Melanie Smith from the Association of Parliamentary Procedures to be the guest speaker for the ceremony.
STEP_10.INCORRECT_1: We have found a guest speaker for our ceremony, but they are unable to commit to the date. I have penciled them in for now.
STEP_10.INCORRECT_2: We are still trying to find a guest speaker for the ceremony. Luke, didn't you say your mom is a doctor? Would she be willing to speak?

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It disregards the value of structured communication by presenting an unconfirmed update without clear follow-up.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks professionalism and preparation, and undermines the importance of planned communication during announcements.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. These are optional parts of a meeting. Thus, announcements can be shared, or any special programs can be held for the group.

ThinkAbout: How do clear announcements reflect preparedness and professionalism in a meeting?
What happens when important announcements are vague, uncertain, or handled informally?
AskYourself: Am I presenting information in a way that maintains order, clarity, and confidence in leadership?
How can well-prepared announcements contribute to a more effective and goal-oriented meeting?

STEP_10.reportRational: These are optional parts of a meeting. Thus, announcements can be shared, or any special programs can be held for the group.

STEP_11.instructions: The meeting has now reached its end with no more items in the agenda to discuss. The group looks exhausted and wants the meeting to adjourn quickly.
instructionsList: Choose the most appropriate course of action in this scenario from the three options provided to you.
Refer to the hint, if you need guidance.
STEP_11.question: What should the group members do?
STEP_11.CORRECT: The president calls for the meeting to end, and a member makes a motion for the meeting to be adjourned. The motion is seconded, voted on, and approved. The president announces, "The meeting is dismissed."
STEP_11.INCORRECT_1: The secretary informs the president that it is now 3:00 pm and time to end the meeting. The president bangs his gavel and announces, "The meeting is adjourned."
STEP_11.INCORRECT_2: The president announces, "We are out of time. We will reserve any unfinished business for our next meeting." He then bangs his gavel and says, "The meeting is adjourned."

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks integrity and structure, and skips the necessary steps to properly adjourn a meeting.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. Although it acknowledges time limits, it skips the motion and voting process required to formally adjourn the meeting.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. A meeting is adjourned after all business is completed or time is over for the meeting. The chair or any member can call for a motion for the meeting to end.

ThinkAbout: How should a meeting officially come to a close?
What steps help ensure everyone is aware that the meeting has ended properly?
AskYourself: Am I ensuring the meeting ends with clarity, order, and agreement from the group?
Why might a structured ending matter just as much as a structured beginning?

STEP_11.reportRational: A meeting is adjourned after all business is completed or time is over for the meeting. The chair or any member can call for a motion for the meeting to end.
